column3: “Which he saw” is rendered “which he envisioned in visions,” and “sheep-tenders” “sheepherders.”
“Dry up” (or “mourn”) is rendered “mourn,” and “wither” “dries up”; NASB uses the present tense.
NASB supplies “its punishment” for “it”; “threshing sledges of iron” is rendered “implements of sharp iron.”
“Bar” is rendered “gate bar”; “into exile to Kir” is rendered “exiled to Kir.”
NASB supplies “its punishment”; “carried away an entire exile” is rendered “deported an entire population.”
“Turn my hand” is rendered “unleash My power.”
NASB supplies “its punishment”; “a complete exile” is rendered “an entire population,” and “covenant of brothers” “covenant of brotherhood.”
NASB supplies “its punishment”; “spoiled his compassions” is rendered “stifled his compassion,” and NASB adds “While.”
NASB supplies “its punishment”; “people of Ammon” is rendered “sons of Ammon.”
“Shout of alarm” is rendered “war cries,” and “storm-wind” “tempest.”
